title: Cross-train launch conductor: unified calendar, signal bus, and contingency matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create a single operational 'launch conductor' playbook and calendar that coordinates runtime, console, and API surface launches. This ticket scopes the end-to-end orchestration: a shared calendar, an event/signal bus for cutover health checks, a contingency matrix for capacity and rollback decisions, and a lightweight comms + ownership roster for week-of-go-live. The conductor should make cross-team cutovers predictable while preserving per-surface autonomy (you can still run independent canaries).

Why this now: recent rollouts exposed gaps where runtime kernel changes impacted console explorer queries during regional rollouts and caused unnecessary rollbacks. We need an explicit, machine-readable signal exchange (signal bus) and a standardized contingency matrix so release leads make consistent decisions under pressure.

Scope:
- Design calendar data model and conventions (slot duration, stakeholder tags, blackout zones).
- Define minimal signal bus schema (preflight, canary, smoke, steady-state) and health thresholds.
- Draft contingency matrix (capacity reserve, fallback model variants, region cutover priority).
- Implement a lightweight calendar view in the Launch Console (PM + Eng feature flag) and deliver a runbook + Slack templates.
- Coordinate required telemetry on dashboards (latency p95, 5xx rate, request throughput, token spend delta) and link alerts to rollback/playbook triggers.

Out of scope: automated capacity provisioning, full infra implementation of the bus (we'll prototype with webhooks and a tiny Lambda), private deployments automation (handled later as follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Shared launch calendar schema and example schedule accepted by runtime, console, and API leads
Signal bus JSON schema documented and implemented as webhook prototype with test harness
Contingency matrix with decision gates (metrics + owner) published in Confluence
Launch Console calendar MVP shows coordinated slots and ownership tags behind feature flag
Runbook and Slack escalation templates added to oncall playbook and linked in the ticket
milestones: Prototype signal bus webhooks + test harness (2026-03-04)
Launch Console calendar MVP behind FF (2026-03-11)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signal noise causing false rollbacks — Mitigation: require 2/3 signals (runtime, console, api) plus threshold change > delta before auto-trigger
Risk: Owners unclear at 2am — Mitigation: explicit roster with primary + secondary and Slack pager rotations in runbook
Risk: Capacity under-provisioned for simultaneous canaries — Mitigation: capacity hedge lanes and preflight load generator to validate slot
tradeoffs: Staggered vs simultaneous canaries: staggered reduces blast radius but increases calendar tail; we standardize a default stagger with opt-in simultaneous for high-confidence patches
Automated rollback vs manual human confirmation: prefer semi-automated triggers (automated alert + required ack from owner within 10 minutes) for initial rollout to avoid noisy auto-rollback
notes: Short-term prototype uses webhook signal bus (Lambda + small SQS buffer) and a simple feature-flagged calendar UI in Launch Console. Longer term we can move to kafka/event-mesh and tighter runbook automation. See linked artifacts for proto details.
